source: Literature review and gap analysis of the thesis draft (Chapter 2, Tables 2.1 and 2.2), plus the demography papers read on 2026-11-25. Descriptions are summaries; numbers are as reported by each study.

themes.name: Dialect identification beyond Bangla
themes.summary: Dialect identification stays hard even with large multi-speaker corpora and strong encoders; combining two views of the signal helps.

themes.name: Bangla dialect and accent
themes.summary: Reported scores range from 75% to above 95%, but every split mixes clips of the same speakers across training and test.

themes.name: Age and gender from speech
themes.summary: Gender is above 90% almost everywhere; age is markedly harder, and Common Voice labels are self-reported and noisy.

themes.name: Fusing two views of the same audio
themes.summary: A spectral CNN and a temporal model capture different information; simple concatenation works as well as complex fusion.

themes.name: Evaluation protocol
themes.summary: The most conservative numbers come from studies that keep test speakers out of training and report confidence intervals.

themes.name: Fairness and inclusion
themes.summary: Speech systems fail more often for dialect and accent speakers, and average accuracy hides those per-group failures.

studies.title: Automatic dialect detection in Arabic broadcast speech
studies.method: Lexical, phonetic and i-vector features with an SVM back end; score fusion; 5 Arabic dialects
studies.findings: 5-way accuracy about 60%; fusion of feature types helps
studies.speakers: Yes: test set from other channels and speakers

studies.title: Aggregated wav2vec 2.0 features and dual-stream TDNN for spoken dialect identification
studies.method: All-layer wav2vec 2.0 aggregation; global and local TDNN streams; Indian dialects
studies.findings: Aggregated self-supervised features beat single layers; dual-stream TDNN beats x-vector baselines

studies.title: Exploring the impact of back-end network on wav2vec 2.0 for dialect identification
studies.method: XLS-R features with spectral and temporal graph-attention back ends; Chinese dialects
studies.findings: Back end halves the error of mean pooling (Cavg 0.030 vs 0.065)

studies.title: Jointly improving dialect identification and ASR in Indian languages using multimodal feature fusion
studies.method: IndicWav2Vec + Conformer; gated acoustic and text-like fusion; RESPIN, 8 languages, 33 dialects
studies.findings: Average dialect accuracy 81.6%; Bengali only 74.5%

studies.title: BengDiDa dataset and Bengali dialect classification
studies.method: 48,000 ten-second social-media clips, 20 dialects; CNN-BiGRU and ResNet-50 + BiGRU
studies.findings: 90.3% (CNN-BiGRU); ResNet-50 + BiGRU 80.8% frozen, 85.3% fine-tuned

studies.title: Multi-label extreme learning machines for Bangla regional speech recognition
studies.venue: Applied Sciences (and Hossain's M.Sc. thesis, BRAC)
studies.method: Stacked convolutional autoencoder + multi-label ELMs; own 30 h corpus, 7 regions; dialect, age and gender together
studies.findings: Dialect 85%, 95% when the age class is used; gender 92%; age 91%

studies.title: Artificial neural networks to recognize speakers' division from continuous Bengali speech
studies.method: MFCC + dense network; 45 h from 633 speakers; 8 divisions
studies.findings: 85.4% validation accuracy

studies.title: BanglaDialecto: end-to-end regional speech standardization
studies.method: Whisper ASR, BanglaT5 translation and TTS for Noakhali speech; 24 readers of one paragraph
studies.findings: Character error rate 0.8%, word error rate 1.5%
studies.speakers: No: random split, same text for everyone

studies.title: A hybrid deep learning approach for dialect-specific sentiment analysis of Bangla regional linguistics
studies.method: Hybrid CNN-LSTM for sentiment; Naive Bayes for dialect; text data
studies.findings: Sentiment accuracy 94.69%

studies.title: Gender and age estimation methods based on speech using deep neural networks
studies.method: x-vector, d-vector and QuartzNet embeddings; Common Voice English, then TIMIT
studies.findings: Gender 99.6% on TIMIT; age error about 5 years; forgetting after fine-tuning
studies.speakers: Partly: authors warn their Common Voice split may share speakers

studies.title: Speech-based age and gender prediction with transformers
studies.method: wav2vec 2.0 with age and gender heads; 4 corpora
studies.findings: Joint model equals separate models; gender at least 91%; age error grows 4-5 years across corpora

studies.title: Demographic attributes prediction from speech using WavLM embeddings
studies.method: Frozen WavLM with MLP, ResNet and BiLSTM heads; 5 corpora including Common Voice
studies.findings: Gender up to 99.8%; accent 61-63%; Common Voice among the weakest (self-reported labels)

studies.title: Layer-wise analysis of self-supervised representations for age and gender in children's speech
studies.method: Frozen wav2vec 2.0 layers with a small CNN
studies.findings: Early layers carry speaker traits; MFCCs already strong for gender

studies.title: CoLMbo: speaker language model for descriptive profiling
studies.method: Frozen speaker encoder + mapper + GPT-2; dialect, gender and age together
studies.findings: Dialect 88.6%; a 25 M-parameter model beats a 7.7 B audio language model; noise augmentation helps age

studies.title: Acoustic analysis of speech for gender and age classification using CNN and machine learning
studies.method: 22 hand-made features + 1D CNN; English Common Voice (not Bangla); 5 age groups
studies.findings: Age 88.1%, gender 96.9%

studies.title: Age and gender recognition from Bengali speech (MFCC + GMM)
studies.method: MFCC + Gaussian mixture models; SHRUTI corpus, 34 speakers; age cut at 30
studies.findings: Gender 88%, age 76% on 34 speaker decisions (95% range about 60-88%)

studies.title: Bengali Common Voice speech dataset for automatic speech recognition
studies.method: Common Voice Bangla v9: 399 h, about 20,000 speakers; ASR baselines
studies.findings: About 84% of training audio is male; age and gender only from logged-in contributors

studies.title: Age and gender effects on voice range profile in Bengali adult speakers (phonetogram)
studies.method: Clinical phonetogram measurements
studies.findings: Age and gender shift the pitch range of Bengali voices

studies.title: Waveforms and spectrograms: multimodal feature fusion for acoustic scene classification
studies.method: 2D CNN on log-mel + 1D CNN on waveform; late fusion; parameter-matched ablation
studies.findings: Fusion 70.8% vs 66.5% and 64.8% for single branches; concatenation as good as other fusions

studies.title: A two-stream convolution architecture for environmental sound classification
studies.method: One MFCC input split into time and frequency streams
studies.findings: Combined streams best; the two streams make different errors

studies.title: Environmental sound classification using feature fusion and data enhancement
studies.method: Seven fused spectral features; 1D CNN and Transformer; noise, pitch and stretch augmentation
studies.findings: Up to 0.98 accuracy (UrbanSound8K)

studies.title: Sound event detection with CNN-Transformer and automatic threshold optimization
studies.method: CNN, CNN-BiGRU and CNN-Transformer on weak labels
studies.findings: CNN-Transformer about equal to CNN + recurrent layer

studies.title: Music genre classification with a transformer-enhanced convolutional recurrent network
studies.method: CNN on mel spectrograms + BiLSTM + attention, fused with handcrafted features
studies.findings: 93.3%; removing fusion costs 4.0 points, removing the BiLSTM 2.6 points

studies.title: Recognizing every voice: towards inclusive ASR for rural Bhojpuri women (SRUTI)
studies.method: Speaker-disjoint benchmark of 51 speakers; synthetic speech from 100 women
studies.findings: Word error rate 33.8 to 29.1 with synthetic data; 15 h left out because it shared speakers

studies.title: Racial disparities in automated speech recognition
studies.method: 5 commercial recognisers; matched Black and white speakers
studies.findings: Word error rate 0.35 vs 0.19; the gap grows with dialect density

studies.title: Training and typological bias in ASR performance for world Englishes
studies.method: Commercial ASR on 24 English varieties; mixed-effects analysis
studies.findings: Unsupported varieties 0.135 vs 0.071 word error rate; Bengali-L1 speakers 0.129

studies.title: Evaluating bias in phoneme-based ASR: IPA transcription models
studies.method: 2 IPA recognisers, 11 languages including Bangla; bootstrap confidence intervals
studies.findings: Accent and dialect are the most robust axis of disparity

studies.title: Addressing accent disparities in ASR: single vs two-step adaptation
studies.method: Whisper and XLSR on AfriSpeech; word error rate gaps with confidence intervals
studies.findings: Average error falls after fine-tuning, but accent gaps remain

studies.title: Systematic review on bias in ASR for low-resource African languages
studies.method: PRISMA systematic review
studies.findings: Dialect, accent, gender and age bias; mitigation is mostly more data, augmentation and transfer learning

gaps.literature: No Bangla study predicts dialect, gender and age with one audio-only model that uses transfer learning for gender and age; the only joint Bangla model needed a corpus with all three labels.
gaps.here: One ResNet-50 + Bi-LSTM network with three outputs. Gender and age are learned from Common Voice, so no Bangla dialect corpus needs those labels.

gaps.gap: Testing on speakers kept out of training
gaps.literature: Every Bangla dialect study reviewed splits clips or segments at random; none tests on unseen speakers, although that is standard in the age, gender and accent literature.
gaps.here: Dialect is tested on RegSpeech12 voice groups held out from training; gender and age on 109 (and 219) Common Voice speakers held out from training; BanglaAccent is a third corpus used only for testing.

gaps.literature: No study checks whether its dialect labels can be told apart from who is speaking.
gaps.here: RBVD has one reader per district, so dialect equals speaker there: an unseen Rangpur speaker was recognised 0% of the time. A separate leakage check found no repeated voices between RegSpeech12 training and test groups.

gaps.literature: Fusing a spectral CNN with a temporal recurrent branch is well supported outside speech, but no Bangla dialect study reports what each branch adds.
gaps.here: Removing the Bi-LSTM branch drops sentence-disjoint macro-F1 from 0.987 to 0.929 (95% range of the difference +4.4 to +7.2 points); removing the ResNet-50 branch leaves 0.981, a difference within chance.
